after: ## Which types of retailer does the syllabus name? (2.3.1)
alt: Retailers sorted by scale. Small-scale: itinerant retailers, independent retailers, street markets and many speciality shops. Large-scale: multiple chain stores, supermarkets, hypermarkets and department stores. Vending machines and online retailers can be either.
caption: Most retailer types sit clearly on one side; vending machines and online retailers can be either.

after: ## Which types of retailer does the syllabus name? (2.3.1)
alt: Four columns compare a multiple chain store, a supermarket, a hypermarket and a department store by their features, one advantage and one disadvantage.
caption: Each large-scale retailer has distinctive features; name them, not just its size.

after: ## Why does the small-scale retailer often survive? (2.3.1)
alt: A small-scale retailer survives through three syllabus examples: personal service, flexible opening hours and additional services such as delivery or informal credit. Convenience and local products are further reasons.
caption: Turn each reason into an explanation of what the small shop does that a large store cannot.

after: ## What selling techniques do retailers use? (2.3.2)
alt: The eleven selling techniques grouped by how they help sales: recognition (branding, logos, packaging), price and cost (own brands, self service), loyalty (loyalty programmes, direct mail, informal credit), confidence (after-sales service, cash on delivery) and speed (barcoding).
caption: Name the technique, then say how it raises sales or loyalty for the retailer.

after: ## What are the digital retail trends? (2.3.3)
alt: Left: in multi-channel retailing the shop, website and app each have their own stock and prices. Right: in omnichannel retailing every channel links to shared stock and one customer account. Below, one journey: check stock in the app, reserve online, collect in store, return by post.
caption: Omnichannel joins the channels up; multi-channel only runs several side by side.

after: ## What are the digital retail trends? (2.3.3)
alt: Dropshipping: the customer orders from the retailer, the retailer passes the order to the supplier, and the supplier sends the goods straight to the customer, so the retailer holds no stock. Click and collect: the customer orders online and picks up from a store or collection point.
caption: A dropshipper never holds the goods; with click and collect the customer fetches them.

after: ## Worked example: an annotated model answer
alt: Two reasons, each worth two marks: name personal service and explain it by contrast with the hypermarket, then name flexible opening hours and explain why they suit customers when the hypermarket needs a car journey.
caption: Name each reason for one mark, then explain it against the hypermarket for the second.
